dedupe_keys.name: taiwan mobile broadband speed measurements by district and operator moda with earlier ncc drive fixed point and consumer tests

description: Taiwan runs a national mobile broadband performance measurement programme to track the service delivered by operators. The Ministry of Digital Affairs publishes the 2022 to 2023 rounds as a public-domain (CC0) dataset of ten CSV files. For each county and district, the files give measured average download and upload speeds in Mbps for each operator: FarEasTone, Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile and, before its merger, Taiwan Star. Before the task moved to the ministry, the National Communications Commission published three measurement series that are no longer updated: consumer-side measurements by county in two phases, fixed-point measurements at named test sites, and mobile drive-route measurements, each with download and upload averages by operator (including the former Asia Pacific Telecom and VIBO). Coverage: Taiwan, by district and operator. Format and access: CSV from the national open data portal, free; the MODA files are CC0 and the NCC files use the Open Government Data License. Caveats: the rounds are periodic campaigns, not continuous monitoring; the method, sample sizes and test dates were not described in the catalogue; the older NCC tables mix phases and operators that no longer exist. Simulation uses: district-level delivered speed baselines by operator for service-quality models, and checks on rural-urban gaps. Related records: the Korea 5G service quality evaluation, the TRAI independent drive tests and the Speedtest by Ookla performance maps give comparable measured speeds.
